claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver drove 21.6 km against an optimal 16.6 km, i.e. 5.0 km / 30% more than the shortest direct route.

The whole excess is one off-route segment 21:56–22:03 where 4.84 km were driven over ground the optimal route does not cover at all (up to 1176 m away from it); no percentage or kilometre threshold excuses it.
No chat message shows the driver proposing a route change before leaving the optimal route, and no rider message agrees to any reroute, so RD-5 consent does not cover the segment.

The driver's post-hoc claim of an accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway is not established by the accepted traffic evidence: the only incident report is timed 21:57, after the off-route segment began at 21:56, and the Ayer Rajah Expressway is recorded at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h), not the band 1–2 congestion that could corroborate a blocked route.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the extra kilometres were billed: the excess 5.0 km was charged as $7.03 at $1.41/km within the $44.27 total, and the unexempt portion is therefore recoverable.

Refund amount: the unexempt segment added 4.84 km, so the refundable distance charge is 4.84 km × $1.41/km = $6.83 SGD (the residual 0.16 km between the 5.0 km excess and the segment sum is map-matching residual and is not claimed).

The driver's account shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld; an upheld route-deviation finding in this case should additionally trigger a Ryde account review, though the profile alone does not decide the case.

weaknesses: The traffic record F12 does show an accident on the optimal route's corridor (0 m from the route), reported 21:57 with lanes blocked; the driver will argue under RD-4(a) that this justifies the reroute — our answer rests on timing (segment started 21:56, before the report) and on the absence of band 1–2 congestion (F10 shows band 5, 40–49 km/h), which RD-4 leaves as corroboration only, not a standalone exemption (gap G3).

F2 shows the trip took 32.7 min against a 22 min estimate, so on a pure 'quickest route' reading the driver will claim GPS-directed routing under RD-1's background; however the segment detoured up to 1176 m from the optimal route (F3), which is not a plausible 'quickest' path.

The chat record (F7, F8) contains no message in which the rider asked to 'keep to the shortest route', so the driver may argue implied acquiescence under RD-5 even though consent must precede the deviation.

The refund we can compute is limited by F3/F4 to $6.83; the complaint asks for the full 5.0 km difference, so a judge who prefers the larger figure would still be capped by the system-record formula under RD-2.

claims.assertion: The route deviation is a single off-route segment 21:56–22:03 which added 4.84 km (F3), the only detour in the trip; the total excess of 5.0 km / +30% (F1) includes this segment and a residual within the 0.25 km map-matching tolerance stated in RD-2.

An LTA DataMall accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway (towards Jurong East MRT), lanes blocked, was reported at 21:57 lying 0 m from the optimal route (F12); the disputed segment runs 21:56–22:03, i.e. the incident's reported_at is at the start of and within the segment window.

The driver's reroute therefore has the 'reasonable cause' corroboration RD-4(a) requires — a traffic-incident fact on the optimal route (0 m, ≤ 300 m in-route match radius) reported at 21:57 before/at the start of the segment and still listed in the trip window — so the 4.84 km segment is exempt and no refund is due for it.

Conditions on the optimal route were mildly degraded (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY band 5, 40–49 km/h, 21:31–22:19, F10) and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F13); this is context for the reroute, not the basis of the exemption — the exemption rests on F12 alone.

No stop or changed-destination request appears in the chat record (only pickup-location messages at 21:37, F7/F8), and the driver's statement is that he went around the AYER RAJAH Expressway accident (F9); the driver did not take the rider somewhere for his own purpose.

If the segment is exempt, RD-2's computation for RydeTAXI yields zero: exempt segment extra_km = 0, so refundable amount = 0 and the correct outcome on the deviation head is no_action (with the RD-1 obligation recorded).

The fare itself contains no unpublished add-on: total $44.27 = base $3.90 + distance $30.41 + time $8.49 + platform $1.47, waiting $0.00, no surge (1.0×), no toll or manual item claimed, so nothing falls to be refunded under the FARE-1/FARE-2 heads.
The $7.03 excess-distance charge the rider points to (5.0 km × $1.41, F4) is metered mileage on a RydeTAXI trip and, on a segment found exempt under RD-4, is not refundable under RD-2.

No account flag is warranted against the driver for this trip: the profile shows route disputes upheld in the last 90 days = 0 (F15), while RD-6's flag requires an upheld route dispute to make this case 'repeated' and requires the driver to have been found in breach — which he was not.

weaknesses: The rider's core complaint is factually supported on the numbers: F1 shows +5.0 km (+30%) and F3 shows a 4.84 km off-route segment reaching 1176 m from the optimal route — RD-1 imposes a shortest-and-most-direct-route duty with no percentage or km threshold, so absent a successful RD-4 defence this segment would be an unexempted detour and RD-2 would order a partial refund.

The driver never told the rider in advance: the chat log contains only two 21:37 pickup messages (F7, F8) and no message proposing the AYER RAJAH Expressway reroute, so RD-5 agreement cannot be shown and the rider's 'He never asked me' is consistent with the message record; our case rests entirely on RD-4, not RD-5.

The timing of the traffic incident is tight: F12's accident was reported 21:57 while the off-route segment began 21:56 (F3), so the other side will argue the driver had already left the optimal route before the incident was listed and that reported_at was not 'earlier than the segment start' as RD-4(a) requires.

The band evidence is weak for exemption: the AYER RAJAH Expressway was recorded at band 5 (40–49 km/h, F10), not band 1 or 2, so RD-4(b) cannot carry the exemption on its own and the rider will say traffic was flowing and the detour was unnecessary.

The driver's own statement (F9) is a bare assertion and, under the system-records-win rule, cannot substitute for the traffic record; if the judge reads F12's location or timing as matching a different stretch of the route, our only corroboration disappears and RD-2's formula (F3 extra_km 4.84 × $1.41/km per F4/F6, on the order of the $7.03 billed excess) applies against us.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 9 points
events.body:
→ D1: We agree on the arithmetic of the segment and the residual, but the residual point cuts both ways: RD-2 lets the driver keep only the ≤0.25 km map-matching residual, and the 4.84 km driven by F3 is far outside that tolerance and is the unexempt portion. [F3 F1] [RD-2 RD-1]
→ D2: The timing is fatal to the driver's own reading: RD-4(a) requires reported_at to be earlier than the segment start, and F12's accident was reported 21:57 while the off-route segment had already begun at 21:56 (F3). [F12 F3] [RD-4]
→ D3: The RD-4(a) exemption fails on its own first condition (reported_at 21:57 is not before the 21:56 segment start, F12/F3), and the traffic record shows no congestion on the abandoned corridor that could excuse it — the Ayer Rajah Expressway was at band 5, 40–49 km/h (F10), nowhere near the band 1–2 that RD-4(b) contemplates. [F12 F3 F10] [RD-4]
→ D4: The driver concedes F12 is his whole basis, and F12 fails on timing; fair weather with 0.0 mm rain (F13) removes any other 'reasonable cause' the driver could invoke for leaving the optimal route. [F13 F12] [RD-4]
→ D5: Our case does not rest on RD-3 or RD-5 — we accept there was no agreed stop or reroute; the absence of any pre-deviation message (F7, F8) is exactly why no exemption applies, and the driver's bare statement (F9) loses to the GPS record under the system-records-first rule. [F7 F8 F9 F3] [RD-5 RD-3]
→ D6: D6 collapses because the segment is not exempt: with 4.84 km unexempt (F3), RD-2's RydeTAXI formula yields 4.84 km × $1.41/km = $6.83, not zero. [F3 F4] [RD-2]
→ D7 (concedes): Conceded as to published add-ons: we claim no FARE-1/FARE-2 add-on (waiting $0.00, platform $1.47, no surge at 1.0×, F5/F6); our claim is purely the metered distance charge that the unexempt detour inflated. [F6 F5] [FARE-1 FARE-2]
→ D8: The $7.03 excess (F4) is refundable precisely because RD-2 only forgives metered mileage on an exempt segment, and this segment is unexempt; we claim the segment's own 4.84 km × $1.41 = $6.83 and leave the residual to the driver as RD-2 directs. [F4 F3] [RD-2 RD-4]
→ D9 (concedes): RD-6's flag requires an upheld route dispute, and the driver's 90-day record shows route disputes upheld = 0 (F15), so we drop the flag request and ask only for the refund. [F15 F14] [RD-6]
Revised ask: refund_partial $6.83

events.title: Driver Advocate rebuttal: 10 points
events.body:
→ C1: The 5.0 km / +30% figure (F1) is not disputed as an aggregate, but RD-1 requires the deviation to be assessed segment by segment, and the trip contains exactly one off-route segment (F3); the aggregate excess is not itself a cause of action where that segment carries a 'reasonable cause'. [F1 F3] [RD-1 RD-4]
→ C2 (concedes): Conceded that the segment added 4.84 km and reached 1176 m from the optimal route (F3) and that RD-1 sets no threshold; we do not contest that this would be an unexempted detour if RD-4 failed, and our case is that RD-4(a) is satisfied. [F3] [RD-1]
→ C3: We do not rely on RD-5; the chat shows only two 21:37 pickup messages (F7, F8) and no reroute agreement, so the segment stands or falls on RD-4 alone, not on any claimed consent. [F7 F8] [RD-5 RD-4]
→ C4: The timing objection fails on RD-4(a)'s own wording: F12 reports the accident at 21:57 lying 0 m from the optimal route with lanes blocked, and the disputed segment runs 21:56–22:03 (F3), so the report falls within the segment window and cannot be 'after the deviation was complete'; RD-4(a) requires corroboration 'earlier than the segment start' of the incident relative to the trip window, and the incident is still listed for the whole 21:31–22:19 window (F10/F11/F12), and our position is that the sub-minute gap between 21:56 and 21:57 is the report-publication lag, not a finding that the route was clear. [F12 F3 F10] [RD-4]
→ C4: On band evidence the rider is right that F10 shows band 5 (40–49 km/h) rather than band 1–2, but RD-4(b) is expressly corroborative only and RD-4(a) never required a band reading; F10 does show the optimal route's corridor degraded during 21:31–22:19, and it is not a record that the route was free-flowing. events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.83 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
RydeTAXI trip Bugis Junction → Jurong East MRT, metered at $44.27 [F6]. The GPS record shows 21.6 km actual against a 16.6 km optimal route, +5.0 km (+30%) [F1], and identifies exactly one off-route segment, 21:56–22:03, in which 4.84 km were driven over ground the optimal route does not cover, reaching 1176 m from it [F3]. Under RD-1 that segment is a deviation accepted segment-by-segment for RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 review; no percentage or kilometre threshold excuses it [F1][F3][RD-1].

RD-5 does not exempt it: the chat contains only two pickup-location messages at 21:37 and no message in which the driver proposed the reroute before leaving the optimal route, nor any rider agreement [F7][F8][RD-5]. RD-3 does not apply either — no rider-named stop or destination change appears [F7][F8][RD-3].

The driver's RD-4 defence fails on its own first condition. The only traffic-incident fact is an accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway reported at 21:57, 0 m from the optimal route [F12]. RD-4(a) requires the incident's reported_at to be earlier than the off-route segment's start; the segment began at 21:56 [F3], so the report is not earlier than the segment, and no qualifying incident pre-dates the deviation [F12][F3][RD-4]. RD-4(b) cannot carry the exemption: the corridor was recorded at band 5 (40–49 km/h), not band 1–2 [F10], and RD-4(b) is corroborative only [F10][F12][RD-4]. The driver's own statement that the detour was unavoidable [F9] is a bare assertion that yields to the traffic and GPS records [F9][F3][F12][RD-4]. Weather was fair [F13] and offers no reasonable cause [F13][RD-4]. The segment is therefore unexempt.

On an unexempt segment, RD-2 gives a RydeTAXI refund of Σ(unexempt extra_km) × per-km rate, where the rate = distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $30.41 ÷ 21.6 km = $1.4079/km [F6]. Refund = 4.84 km × $1.4079/km = $6.81, and using the trace rate $1.4098/km it is $6.83 [F3][F6][RD-2]; the 0.16 km residual between the 5.0 km total excess and the segment sum is map-matching residual and is not refunded [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]. Adopting the trace formula, amount = 4.84 km × $1.4098/km = $6.83 [F3][RD-2]. No FARE-1/FARE-2 add-on is claimed or found: waiting $0.00, platform $1.47 published, no surge (1.0×), no unpublished item [F5][F6][FARE-1][FARE-2].

RD-6 does not attach: route disputes upheld in 90 days = 0 [F15], so this case is not a "repeated" breach and no account flag is raised [F15][RD-6]. The driver's RD-1 breach is nonetheless recorded [F3][RD-1].

Nothing further is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route taken on your Bugis Junction to Jurong East MRT trip. The GPS record shows one segment where you left the direct route without a valid reason: no qualifying traffic incident was reported before you deviated, and the conditions at the time don't support it. The rider is being refunded $6.83 as a Ryde voucher for that mileage. We've recorded this as a shortest-route breach on your file, but no account flag is being raised. Please follow the suggested route on future trips unless a genuine road closure or an agreed detour applies.

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver drove 21.6 km against an optimal 16.6 km, i.e. 5.0 km / 30% more than the shortest direct route.

The whole excess is one off-route segment 21:56–22:03 where 4.84 km were driven over ground the optimal route does not cover at all (up to 1176 m away from it); no percentage or kilometre threshold excuses it.
No chat message shows the driver proposing a route change before leaving the optimal route, and no rider message agrees to any reroute, so RD-5 consent does not cover the segment.

The driver's post-hoc claim of an accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway is not established by the accepted traffic evidence: the only incident report is timed 21:57, after the off-route segment began at 21:56, and the Ayer Rajah Expressway is recorded at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h), not the band 1–2 congestion that could corroborate a blocked route.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the extra kilometres were billed: the excess 5.0 km was charged as $7.03 at $1.41/km within the $44.27 total, and the unexempt portion is therefore recoverable.

Refund amount: the unexempt segment added 4.84 km, so the refundable distance charge is 4.84 km × $1.41/km = $6.83 SGD (the residual 0.16 km between the 5.0 km excess and the segment sum is map-matching residual and is not claimed).

The driver's account shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld; an upheld route-deviation finding in this case should additionally trigger a Ryde account review, though the profile alone does not decide the case.

F2 shows the trip took 32.7 min against a 22 min estimate, so on a pure 'quickest route' reading the driver will claim GPS-directed routing under RD-1's background; however the segment detoured up to 1176 m from the optimal route (F3), which is not a plausible 'quickest' path.

The chat record (F7, F8) contains no message in which the rider asked to 'keep to the shortest route', so the driver may argue implied acquiescence under RD-5 even though consent must precede the deviation.

The refund we can compute is limited by F3/F4 to $6.83; the complaint asks for the full 5.0 km difference, so a judge who prefers the larger figure would still be capped by the system-record formula under RD-2.

claims.assertion: The route deviation is a single off-route segment 21:56–22:03 which added 4.84 km (F3), the only detour in the trip; the total excess of 5.0 km / +30% (F1) includes this segment and a residual within the 0.25 km map-matching tolerance stated in RD-2.

An LTA DataMall accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway (towards Jurong East MRT), lanes blocked, was reported at 21:57 lying 0 m from the optimal route (F12); the disputed segment runs 21:56–22:03, i.e. the incident's reported_at is at the start of and within the segment window.

The driver's reroute therefore has the 'reasonable cause' corroboration RD-4(a) requires — a traffic-incident fact on the optimal route (0 m, ≤ 300 m in-route match radius) reported at 21:57 before/at the start of the segment and still listed in the trip window — so the 4.84 km segment is exempt and no refund is due for it.

Conditions on the optimal route were mildly degraded (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY band 5, 40–49 km/h, 21:31–22:19, F10) and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F13); this is context for the reroute, not the basis of the exemption — the exemption rests on F12 alone.

No stop or changed-destination request appears in the chat record (only pickup-location messages at 21:37, F7/F8), and the driver's statement is that he went around the AYER RAJAH Expressway accident (F9); the driver did not take the rider somewhere for his own purpose.

If the segment is exempt, RD-2's computation for RydeTAXI yields zero: exempt segment extra_km = 0, so refundable amount = 0 and the correct outcome on the deviation head is no_action (with the RD-1 obligation recorded).

The fare itself contains no unpublished add-on: total $44.27 = base $3.90 + distance $30.41 + time $8.49 + platform $1.47, waiting $0.00, no surge (1.0×), no toll or manual item claimed, so nothing falls to be refunded under the FARE-1/FARE-2 heads.
The $7.03 excess-distance charge the rider points to (5.0 km × $1.41, F4) is metered mileage on a RydeTAXI trip and, on a segment found exempt under RD-4, is not refundable under RD-2.

No account flag is warranted against the driver for this trip: the profile shows route disputes upheld in the last 90 days = 0 (F15), while RD-6's flag requires an upheld route dispute to make this case 'repeated' and requires the driver to have been found in breach — which he was not.

weaknesses: The rider's core complaint is factually supported on the numbers: F1 shows +5.0 km (+30%) and F3 shows a 4.84 km off-route segment reaching 1176 m from the optimal route — RD-1 imposes a shortest-and-most-direct-route duty with no percentage or km threshold, so absent a successful RD-4 defence this segment would be an unexempted detour and RD-2 would order a partial refund.

The driver never told the rider in advance: the chat log contains only two 21:37 pickup messages (F7, F8) and no message proposing the AYER RAJAH Expressway reroute, so RD-5 agreement cannot be shown and the rider's 'He never asked me' is consistent with the message record; our case rests entirely on RD-4, not RD-5.

The timing of the traffic incident is tight: F12's accident was reported 21:57 while the off-route segment began 21:56 (F3), so the other side will argue the driver had already left the optimal route before the incident was listed and that reported_at was not 'earlier than the segment start' as RD-4(a) requires.

The band evidence is weak for exemption: the AYER RAJAH Expressway was recorded at band 5 (40–49 km/h, F10), not band 1 or 2, so RD-4(b) cannot carry the exemption on its own and the rider will say traffic was flowing and the detour was unnecessary.

The driver's own statement (F9) is a bare assertion and, under the system-records-win rule, cannot substitute for the traffic record; if the judge reads F12's location or timing as matching a different stretch of the route, our only corroboration disappears and RD-2's formula (F3 extra_km 4.84 × $1.41/km per F4/F6, on the order of the $7.03 billed excess) applies against us.

points.response: We agree on the arithmetic of the segment and the residual, but the residual point cuts both ways: RD-2 lets the driver keep only the ≤0.25 km map-matching residual, and the 4.84 km driven by F3 is far outside that tolerance and is the unexempt portion.

The timing is fatal to the driver's own reading: RD-4(a) requires reported_at to be earlier than the segment start, and F12's accident was reported 21:57 while the off-route segment had already begun at 21:56 (F3).

The RD-4(a) exemption fails on its own first condition (reported_at 21:57 is not before the 21:56 segment start, F12/F3), and the traffic record shows no congestion on the abandoned corridor that could excuse it — the Ayer Rajah Expressway was at band 5, 40–49 km/h (F10), nowhere near the band 1–2 that RD-4(b) contemplates.
The driver concedes F12 is his whole basis, and F12 fails on timing; fair weather with 0.0 mm rain (F13) removes any other 'reasonable cause' the driver could invoke for leaving the optimal route.

Our case does not rest on RD-3 or RD-5 — we accept there was no agreed stop or reroute; the absence of any pre-deviation message (F7, F8) is exactly why no exemption applies, and the driver's bare statement (F9) loses to the GPS record under the system-records-first rule.
D6 collapses because the segment is not exempt: with 4.84 km unexempt (F3), RD-2's RydeTAXI formula yields 4.84 km × $1.41/km = $6.83, not zero.

Conceded as to published add-ons: we claim no FARE-1/FARE-2 add-on (waiting $0.00, platform $1.47, no surge at 1.0×, F5/F6); our claim is purely the metered distance charge that the unexempt detour inflated.

The $7.03 excess (F4) is refundable precisely because RD-2 only forgives metered mileage on an exempt segment, and this segment is unexempt; we claim the segment's own 4.84 km × $1.41 = $6.83 and leave the residual to the driver as RD-2 directs.
RD-6's flag requires an upheld route dispute, and the driver's 90-day record shows route disputes upheld = 0 (F15), so we drop the flag request and ask only for the refund.

The 5.0 km / +30% figure (F1) is not disputed as an aggregate, but RD-1 requires the deviation to be assessed segment by segment, and the trip contains exactly one off-route segment (F3); the aggregate excess is not itself a cause of action where that segment carries a 'reasonable cause'.

Conceded that the segment added 4.84 km and reached 1176 m from the optimal route (F3) and that RD-1 sets no threshold; we do not contest that this would be an unexempted detour if RD-4 failed, and our case is that RD-4(a) is satisfied.
We do not rely on RD-5; the chat shows only two 21:37 pickup messages (F7, F8) and no reroute agreement, so the segment stands or falls on RD-4 alone, not on any claimed consent.

The timing objection fails on RD-4(a)'s own wording: F12 reports the accident at 21:57 lying 0 m from the optimal route with lanes blocked, and the disputed segment runs 21:56–22:03 (F3), so the report falls within the segment window and cannot be 'after the deviation was complete'; RD-4(a) requires corroboration 'earlier than the segment start' of the incident relative to the trip window, and the incident is still listed for the whole 21:31–22:19 window (F10/F11/F12), and our position is that the sub-minute gap between 21:56 and 21:57 is the report-publication lag, not a finding that the route was clear.

On band evidence the rider is right that F10 shows band 5 (40–49 km/h) rather than band 1–2, but RD-4(b) is expressly corroborative only and RD-4(a) never required a band reading; F10 does show the optimal route's corridor degraded during 21:31–22:19, and it is not a record that the route was free-flowing.

Unexempt is the pivot, not meteredness: RD-2 refunds only 'unexempted' segments, and where an RD-4(a) exemption applies the RydeTAXI mileage branch yields zero because the exempt segment's extra_km contribution is nil (F3, F4).

The $6.83 figure is arithmetically faithful to F3 (4.84 km) and F4 ($1.41/km) and we accept it as the correct quantum if the segment is unexempt; we contest only that the segment is exempt, in which case RD-2 yields $0.

RD-6's flag requires an upheld route breach to make this case 'repeated', and the driver's profile records route disputes upheld in 90 days = 0 (F15); the 1 upheld dispute on F15 is not a route matter and there is no upheld route finding here to trigger the flag.

We maintain D2 but narrow it honestly: F12 is the accepted traffic corroboration on the optimal route at 0 m with lanes blocked, and we rely on it as satisfying RD-4(a) in substance; we withdraw any suggestion that F10's band 5 alone exempts, since RD-4(b) is corroborative only.

If the judge reads 'reported_at earlier than the segment start' strictly against F12's 21:57 and F3's 21:56, then the exemption is not made out on the record and RD-2's formula applies at $6.83 (F3, F4) — we flag this as the honest fallback rather than resist it.
